component: P2 dead letters, queue dispatch and AI budgets
problem: Dead-letter/budget notifications are log lines. No deployed alert rule, tested delivery or acknowledgment/escalation chain was supplied. Repeated queue dispatch failures keep jobs queued, so they may never generate the dead-letter alert.
failure: Cloud Tasks dispatch stays broken; sweeps log/retry while the user sees queued. Nobody is demonstrably notified, and a saga can remain unmerging indefinitely.
consequence: Missed deadlines and zombie workflows; existing monitoring configuration outside this checkout is unknown.
correction: Provision alerts for dispatch/commit failures, oldest queue/saga age, dead letters, unresolved spend and source freshness. Deliver to a named operator and partner worklist with acknowledgment and escalation; exercise every route through fault injection.
confidence: Log mechanisms verified; actual alert policy NOT DEMONSTRATED

title: Health endpoints can stay HTTP-green during dependency failure
problem: Functions health always returns status ok. Corpus DB failure returns a degraded JSON body with HTTP 200, and each probe traverses PDF files/seen state. Neither establishes queue, provider-accounting or object-store readiness.
failure: A status-only load balancer routes traffic to a service whose database is unavailable; frequent probes scan a growing file vault and add work during an incident.
consequence: Delayed outage detection and avoidable probe overhead.
correction: Provide cheap liveness and separate bounded readiness returning 503 for required dependency failures. Expose cached freshness/queue telemetry rather than recursive file enumeration, and test health under database and dispatch failure.
confidence: Endpoint source verified

title: The embedding representation omits most document content
problem: Embedding input takes only the first 2,000 characters of full_text/section_text and mixes title/citation into one vector. No versioned chunk/page coverage, retrieval ranking evaluation or later-page evidence mapping is implemented on this path.
failure: The controlling paragraph appears late in a long judgment and cannot contribute to its embedding. A completed queue item incorrectly suggests the document was fully represented for semantic retrieval.
consequence: Low recall and misleading retrieval/grounding claims. The public search itself is substring matching, not RAG.
correction: Build versioned, language-aware chunks with page/paragraph anchors and content hashes; evaluate hybrid lexical/vector retrieval on real legal queries, including later-page holdings and Urdu content, before promising document-wide semantic search.
confidence: Representation verified; real retrieval performance NOT DEMONSTRATED

title: Corpus runtime artifacts are mutable and diverge from the pinned test environment
problem: The production requirements have no versions/hashes and images use mutable tags; the 33-test environment pins a different minimal dependency set. A test pass cannot certify future runtime resolution, native parsers or browser packages.
failure: Rebuild weeks later changes SQLAlchemy/parser/browser behavior or introduces an advisory without a source change; binary extraction behavior becomes irreproducible.
consequence: Supply-chain and forensic reproducibility weakness.
correction: Lock production Python dependencies with hashes and image digests, retain an SBOM and parser versions, and test the actual signed image rather than substituting the minimal test environment. Refresh artifacts through controlled upgrades.
confidence: Manifest comparison verified

title: Corpus administration uses one all-powerful shared key
problem: require_admin_api_key authenticates possession of one static key, without named operator identity, distinct scopes, expiry or a demonstrated rotation overlap mechanism. Trigger/export/promotion use the same authority.
failure: A copied dashboard/admin key permits source triggering, bulk exports and promotion. Revoking one operator requires rotating the shared key for everyone, and reviewer attribution cannot be derived from it.
consequence: Weak attribution and broad credential blast radius; constant-time comparison correctly limits timing leakage but not privilege.
correction: Use named short-lived OIDC identities and scoped corpus roles for trigger/review/export; require step-up for publication. Log immutable actor/decision context and test revocation plus key/token rotation without downtime.
confidence: Authentication mechanism verified; no live key exposed

title: Optional eve execution needs a different Node target from CI/Functions
problem: CI uses Node 22 and Functions declares Node 22, while eve requires Node>=24. The Next console can run on Node 22, so this is not proof that the core app cannot build; it is an unresolved optional-agent runtime contract.
failure: An agent developer uses the CI-standard Node version for eve: unsupported-engine behavior appears. Moving all Functions jobs to Node 24 contradicts the deployment engine target.
consequence: Inconsistent agent/deployment reproducibility and misleading single-toolchain setup instructions.
correction: Split the optional eve Node-24 task from Node-22 Functions tests/deploy, pin both toolchains and document activation. Keep eve outside the mandatory production path until its orchestration contract is implemented and validated.
confidence: Engine requirements and install warning verified
